The calculations for electric dipole transition amplitudes involved summing over Regge contributions, with the option to split these into initial, fundamental, and peripheral components. The calculations for the three-body scattering process revealed that the triple Regge rules can be satisfied, with the added ability to break down these rules into corresponding components.

This study explores the first and second equivariant cohomology of the torus, considering a finite group action that incorporates a twist, which is analogous to a concept in elliptic cohomology. Our findings are expressed in terms of the group's order and the generator of $\mathbb{Z}_2$, along with the equivariant cohomology rings of the torus and one-dimensional circle, which are calculated using the Gysin sequence for the one-dimensional circle.

This study presents an approach to elevate the sense of community and collaboration within an academic department's online platforms. By gathering and analyzing data from existing sites, we aim to inform strategies that can improve the overall departmental atmosphere. We offer actionable recommendations for administrators to enhance community spirit and foster collaborative spirit.

This paper examines the fractional series operator's mapping properties. It establishes a precise condition under which the operator is not bounded from $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$ into $H^{q}(\mathbb{Z})}$. Furthermore, an equivalent condition is provided for the operator's compactness within $H^{p}(\mathbb{Z})$.

In non-credible second-price auctions, where bidders' valuations are independently and identically distributed from a uniform distribution, sellers fail to secure the highest revenue possible due to breaking auction rules, even when it is in their best interest. This paper demonstrates that in such situations, sellers' decisions are influenced by two behavioral factors: (1) the fear of losing revenue due to other bidders' higher valuations, and (2) the desire to avoid giving up additional revenue in exchange for minimal gains. These factors are further illustrated through an analysis of the most profitable auction strategies, which are shown to be consistent with observations in real-world auctions.

We explore the possibility that anisotropic extra dimensions in string theory can account for the universe's isotropy, using the FLRW metric for a bulk space-time. Considering a scalar field driving the cosmological evolution, we examine how anisotropy influences the Hubble parameter and, in turn, the anisotropy itself. Notably, our model exhibits a universal isotropy over time, despite anisotropic geometry in extra dimensions. We also investigate the scalar spectral index and the tensor-to-spectral index ratio, finding that our anisotropic geometry can generate a red spectral index and a minimal tensor-spectral ratio, in line with Planck 2018 constraints.

We establish a Gr\"obner basis for the local defining ideal of a Hessenberg variety, specifically in terms of the maximal elements of a Hessenberg family, using a specific monomial order. This Gr\"obner basis consists of generators related to the structures of standard Young tableaux with Hessenberg shapes.

Recent advancements in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have led to the creation of innovative AI art, with the potential to revolutionize the field of computer graphics. This study leverages Conditional GANs to generate realistic brushstrokes for paintings, contributing to the growing literature on generative brushstroke models. By integrating these strokes into a 2D canvas over time, the model produces full paintings, differing from prior approaches that either segment images into individual strokes or generate them independently in a fixed position.

The Republic of China's Taiwan Physics Society and the Institute of Physics held a joint workshop on "Flavor Anomalies and New Physics Below 2-3 TeV." This workshop brought together international and local experts to discuss the latest developments in flavor anomalies, new physics possibilities, and proposed experiments to investigate these areas further. This proceedings article summarizes the key presentations and highlights from the workshop's sessions, focusing on recent progress in the search for new physics and experimental efforts to address these questions.

We introduce QASPER, a large, standardized dataset designed to enhance question answering capabilities in pro/con systems. The dataset consists of over 36,000 annotated conversations, along with nearly 9,000 leading questions that demand opposing answers, and over 28,000 corresponding follow-up questions. The QASPER dataset was created to address the current limitations in existing datasets by focusing on a broader range of topics and incorporating more challenging questions. The dataset will be made available upon acceptance of this paper.

The explosion of a massive star in a core-collapse supernova is not guaranteed, and even if it does explode, the shock front that forms may not always be stable. Using 3D radiation hydrodynamics simulations, we studied the post-shock instability in both exploding and non-exploding scenarios, specifically within the context of a protoneutron star and its immediate surroundings, immediately after the star collapses. We found that in non-exploding scenarios, the shock front becomes unstable almost instantly, while in exploding scenarios, the shock front remains stable due to the protoneutron star's surface. However, we discovered that this stability is short-lived and the shock front eventually becomes unstable as the protoneutron star shrinks. We found that this instability has a characteristic timescale of a few seconds, which could potentially impact the initial spin of the neutron star.

Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder, has been increasingly studied using Deep Learning techniques on functional magnetic resonance imaging data. Current studies rely on the entire fMRI dataset to classify ADHD, although this overlooks the sparse nature of activated brain regions involved in the condition. This paper proposes an end-to-end framework that integrates a saliency model to identify and prioritize regions of interest, then trains a classifier on the reduced set of activated areas. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated by the high accuracy of 70.46%, outperforming existing methods that require the full dataset.

We examine the existence and distinctiveness of the interior fixed point of the non-linear operator resulting from the combination of a convex function with a monotone operator in the Hilbert space $H$.

Acronyms are widespread in written language and often used in various domains such as law, medicine, and engineering, where lengthy phrases are shortened into easier-to-read words. The numerous possible expansions of an acronym complicate identification and disambiguation processes. Existing systems primarily focus on domains for which large datasets, like Wikipedia, are available. This paper proposes a new approach to improve acronym recognition and disambiguation by leveraging context provided by full forms, rather than relying on large datasets. The method utilizes a graph-based model to connect acronyms with their possible full forms and context information. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this context-driven approach in improving acronym recognition and disambiguation.

We suggest a method to accomplish heat rectification in a quantum Hall system. The heat flow from a normal metal to a quantum Hall state is generally in the same direction as the electrical current, however we propose that this can be inverted by incorporating a point contact that couples an additional heat source. The heat from this contact can cause a significant increase in the heat flow in the opposite direction of the electrical current, effectively allowing us to measure the Esaki diode effect through heat measurements.

This paper introduces an innovative approach to partition management within DNA data storage systems, focusing on reducing overhead and ensuring low read errors. We show that current DNA storage architectures can achieve optimal read performance by applying a simple yet efficient primer pair design policy, which maximizes storage capacity. Furthermore, we developed an algorithm to generate pairs of primers that minimize conflicts between storage partitions, thereby reducing the number of read operations required and associated overhead. The algorithm's effectiveness is validated through numerical experiments and an open-source tool.

We have discovered a new type of topological state that manifests as nodal rings in the momentum space. Unlike other topological states, these nodal rings don't appear as gapless points but rather as extensive two-dimensional structures. Our research reveals that they can be found in a wide range of materials, including those with non-Hermitian properties, and are characterized by a specific invariant. Furthermore, we have developed a theoretical framework for generating materials that host nodal rings through artificial design.

We examine the behavior of waves produced by an array of coupled oscillators with a geometric structure that has rotational symmetry. Their speed is determined by how the connections between oscillators depend on the direction from which they are viewed. This connection rule can be represented by a matrix, $A$, whose entries dictate the strength of connections between adjacent oscillators. We find that waves travel faster on certain areas of this network than on others, specifically where the eigenvalues of matrix $A$ exceed 0. Additionally, we identify a relationship between these 'fast' areas and the internal angles of the network's geometric layout.

This paper presents a novel, non-parametric entropy estimation method that builds upon a previous approach by Grunwald-Kiefer, enhancing its capability to handle discrete and continuous data without imposing a minimum input entropy threshold. The modified algorithm is then adapted to develop an unsupervised learning method for recovering discrete source distributions, while ensuring its asymptotic consistency and rate of convergence.

As deep learning technology advances, there is growing interest in developing imaging biobanks to support artificial intelligence research and applications. To meet the evolving needs of users, it is essential to reconsider the design and implementation of these biobanks. This reflection paper identifies key factors to consider when building imaging biobanks, including their original purpose, data variety, associated clinical information, software frameworks, and potential reuse scenarios. The authors also discuss current challenges and present several successful examples of imaging biobanks to inform future design and implementation efforts.

Data augmentation has become a widely used technique to enhance the performance of machine learning models. Although its benefits are well-established in the vision domain, its effectiveness in other fields, such as medical diagnosis, remains unclear. Specifically, we investigate whether data augmentation can improve the accuracy of the Symptom-Phrase Embedding model in predicting primary diagnoses from patient charts. We consider various augmentation methods and feature configurations to understand their impact. Our results indicate that data augmentation is beneficial when the model relies on external clinical features, but it can also be unnecessary or even counterproductive when the model uses only encoded symptoms.

Polymatroidal ideals hold great significance within the realm of algebraic geometry due to their relationship with rational singularities. In the case of a polymatroid with a large number of elements, the total coordinate space becomes a non-normal variety, known example of which is the second secant variety of the Veronese variety. For a general polymatroid, it's unclear whether the ideal generates a non-normal variety. This question is explored in the context of polymatroids with a small number of elements.

We develop a quantum version of the K-means clustering algorithm, taking advantage of quantum computing's capabilities to enhance its efficiency. The asymptotic complexity of our quantum approach is $O(it)$, where $i$ represents the number of iterations and $t$ represents the number of data points. In contrast, the best classical implementation has a complexity of $O(it^2)$. The quantum algorithm significantly outperforms its classical counterpart when the number of data points is substantial.

The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite has greatly increased the number of known planetary events, allowing us to better understand the distribution of planet masses and improve transit models. By analyzing the differences between observed and theoretical transit times, we can identify additional celestial events beyond transiting planets. So far, we have found 11 potential extra signals in the data from 202,000 eclipsing binary stars, indicating a significant increase in the number of known planetary masses. By combining these findings with previous discoveries, we can refine the function that describes the ratio of planet masses and predict the number of planets per star, helping to guide future observational efforts.

Recent advancements in ray tracing have led to significant computational costs, making it impractical for real-time applications. To address this limitation, we present a method for shadow computation that leverages machine learning to reduce computational requirements. Our approach integrates learned geometric primitives to represent scene geometry, which is trained once and can be used to cast shadows in subsequent applications. Compared to traditional ray tracing, our method yields a substantial decrease in computational time, amounting to a 2-6 times performance boost, while maintaining comparable visual quality to classical techniques.

In the context of probabilistic origin-destination demand modeling via the multinomial logit model and a normal-distribution assumption, the available methods typically rely on the maximum-likelihood principle to estimate the origin-destination matrix and the covariance matrix, often using a prior regularization on the covariance matrix's eigenvalues to address the ill-posedness issue. However, this approach is susceptible to being misled by the regularization parameter and may not effectively suppress unnecessary information in the covariance matrix. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel method that incorporates Lasso regularization, which has been proven to be effective in high-dimensional linear regression problems. The Lasso-regularized minimum-contrast estimation (L-MCE) method is proposed for the covariance matrix's estimation, and its asymptotic normality and sparse structure are theoretically demonstrated. The results show that L-MCE outperforms the prior-regularized minimum-contrast estimation (P-MCE) method in terms of estimation efficiency and the amount of information suppressed.

We're examining three coupled oscillators with one being the leader and the others followers, under the influence of incommensurate wave interference. Nonlinear effects are weak but sufficient to alter the system's behavior. In the weak coupling regime, the stable phase-locked states lose stability, whereas the loss of stability in the strong coupling regime is preserved. The system's singularities can be accurately described by a set of equations that incorporate the primary frequency doubling mechanism, and these equations exhibit a unique characteristic of wave phase locking.

We've enhanced the Wilson and Aldous-Broder uniform spanning tree algorithms by combining their efficient and fast-to-average variants. The hybrid method outperforms the original algorithms in terms of time complexity, offering a $O(n)$ improvement with high probability.

Developing robust music representations is crucial for cross-modal retrieval applications. Current datasets, however, rely on automatic music tagging which may not accurately reflect human preferences. In this work, we present the MusicTM-Dataset, a large, multi-modal collection of music based on human-generated lyrics and song titles. This dataset enables the creation of robust music representations through extensive training data. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our dataset in enhancing the performance of music representation learning from various sources.

This case study showcases Ontodia's capabilities in creating interactive visualizations, using a complex dataset of Wikidata to demonstrate its benefits. Wikidata's comprehensive information makes it challenging to display relationships using conventional tools. Ontodia's enhanced experience is particularly evident when exploring data like Wikidata, allowing users to create and view diagrams more efficiently.

This study establishes the orbital stability of black solitons in the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a complex potential, and extends this stability to include traveling dark solitons. The key finding reveals that the stability of black solitons is independent of the wave speed.

The Lotse library is a widely used resource within the Spacecraft Guidance and Control community, implementing various guidance strategies and aiming to replace existing proprietary tools. To maintain its value, the library must adapt to integrate new approaches, specifically deep learning, which has shown great promise in this field. A key benefit of deep learning is its ability to generate control laws with minimal knowledge of the system model. In this research, we present a deep learning-based approach to guidance, which we have successfully integrated into the Lotse library.

This study presents a computational framework for designing magnetic coils that can modify and adapt to existing magnetic fields. The researcher's approach involves identifying key points on a reference flux surface, then adjusting their positions to create a new set of coil currents that yields a revised magnetic field. The paper outlines methods to calculate initial coil positions, optimize them for a target flux surface, and use these points to determine coil currents. The researcher also develops strategies to maintain a stable ratio of coil currents, ensuring the new surface remains nested. The paper showcases its method's effectiveness in modifying a tokamak's magnetic field.

The proton resonance frequency in solid hydrogen-para- and -deuterium-targets changes with temperature, offering a potential method for measuring reactor temperature using the proton recoil beta-particle detection technique. A key factor influencing this measurement will be the temperature-dependent proton resonance frequency shift, which is the primary focus of this study. The study employed Density Functional Theory and Monte Carlo simulations to calculate the proton site occupancy in HD solid solutions as a function of temperature. These calculations were then used to determine the proton resonance frequency in solid HD, which was found to increase with temperature due to changes in the proton binding energy and site availability.

We've developed a model that explains how multiple substances interact and form new, stable states under external pressure. In our model, substances can either resist pressure changes or change state and release energy in response. A mathematical framework that represents the stability of these states exists, and we've shown that this framework has inherent properties that apply universally to all possible states. We've also identified patterns within this framework and used them to understand how new, stable states emerge when substances interact.

We analyzed data from the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory and found that a significant solar flare on January 17, 2017, caused magnetic disturbances moving across two sunspots at speeds between 150-400 km/s. These transients were observed in the 171 Angstrom layer of the sun's atmosphere and were associated with the flare's high-energy emission detected by the X-ray Telescope on board the High-Altitude Astronomical Observatory. We found that the magnetic disturbances in the sunspots were strongest in the 150-300 keV energy range and were powered by the flare's energy release.

The Madsen-Weiss theorem can be seen as a connection between the b-principle and two other important theorems - stability theorems from Gromov and Segal. To break down this connection, we'll use the language of polyhedral complexes to simplify the presentation.

The Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) method is a widely used preconditioner that excels in solving linear systems arising from Navier-Stokes equations in unstructured mesh environments. Despite its effectiveness, the BDDC method's performance is heavily influenced by several parameters, including the degree of nonlocal communication and the choice of residual balancing algorithm. In this study, we conduct an in-depth analysis of these parameters, focusing on their impact on the condition number and convergence rate of the solver. The findings from our numerical experiments are also presented to support the theoretical conclusions.

This research focuses on the behavior of users who participate in open-content projects by creating and editing tags, which can offer valuable insights for the development of new content management systems. To achieve this, we need to identify patterns in users' tag creation and modification activities across various platforms. However, current approaches are hindered by the lack of comprehensive tag data available for scrutiny. This study aims to address this limitation by presenting a new framework that enables the analysis of users' tagging behavior on Wikipedia. By combining natural language processing techniques and network analysis, we can uncover underlying categories of tags and their associated topics. Our results show that tag creation and modification processes exhibit different characteristics and are influenced by distinct factors.

Acoustic metamaterials exhibit unique properties that can be leveraged at various scales, ranging from microscopic to macroscopic sizes. The behavior of these materials is typically described using the linearized compressible Navier-Stokes and heat conduction equations. The study of thermoviscous effects is crucial in the design of low-scale metamaterials, where viscosity and thermal conductivity play a significant role. The analysis involves solving the Navier-Stokes and energy equations in a specific geometry to determine the effective properties of the metamaterial. The results show that thermoviscous effects lead to reduced negative effective properties compared to the classical viscous case.

This study focuses on the low-frequency regime of the FENE dumbbell model, leading to the existence of solutions in specific Besov spaces. Introducing a low-frequency cut-off in the dumbbell model yields a solution with exponential decay in time, existing within a particular space defined by Besov norms. By incorporating a low-frequency condition into the Smoluchowski equation, which governs the alignment distribution, we obtain an exponential decay in time of the Besov norms for the joint distribution of the orientation and the velocity gradient. This enables derivation of the existence of a solution to the FENE dumbbell model, which exhibits exponential decay in time, and which belongs to a particular space defined by Besov norms.

This research introduces a connectivity problem known as mobile integrated access and backhaul (mIAB) grouping. In scenarios where ground moving targets cooperate, forming groups, their combined signal strength can be leveraged to regenerate the missing high-gain channel caused by mobility. A key challenge arises from the varying group sizes and configurations. To address this issue, we develop two methods: the first involves partitioning the search area into grid cells to create mIAB group candidates, while the second employs a clustering technique based on the K-means algorithm. Both methods are evaluated using simulations.

In the field of hyperparameter optimization, researchers have extensively explored the concept of stability. Currently, the understanding of stable hyperparameters is limited to individual effects, disregarding potential interactions between them. By employing a novel approach based on copulas, we are able to measure the joint stability of hyperparameters and reveal that its value significantly exceeds the combined effect of each hyperparameter's own stability. Our research demonstrates the practical utility of copulas in assessing the stability of hyperparameters and also shows that they can be utilized to uncover non-linear relationships among algorithm performance metrics.

The quantization of the electromagnetic field leads to a preclusion of certain transitions within the Balmer series, a consequence arising from the application of the uncertainty principle to wavevectors $k_x$, $k_y$, and $k_z$.

Reinforcement learning algorithms are typically evaluated in static environments, but in many real-world scenarios, they encounter changing educational structures that evolve with newly available information and hidden task objectives. Current evaluation methods are inadequate for assessing adaptability to such dynamic curricula due to their inability to model varied progressions and sudden changes. To address this limitation, we introduce a new approach that generates a sequence of curricula based on an initial diverse range of off-policy data and identifies areas of sudden change within an agent's behavior, enabling the comparison of reinforcement learning algorithms in dynamic environments.

Liger, a next-generation optical/near-optical wavelength astronomical telescope, is under construction at the top of the Mauna Kea mountain in Hawaii. This 39-meter telescope boasts an enormous light-gathering ability, allowing it to observe the universe across a wide range of wavelengths. The Data Reduction System (DRS) is a critical component of Liger, responsible for processing the vast amounts of data generated by the telescope. In this study, we outline the requirements and constraints governing the DRS's operation, as well as its technical specifications.

We investigate the three-dimensional Couette flow within a channel of finite height in a rotating system. The non-paired linear instability is represented by a family of eigenfunctions with varying levels of regularity. Our analysis shows that for any regularity level below three, non-trivial traveling wave solutions exist near the Couette flow. In contrast, we find that this phenomenon is limited to regularity levels below three.

Achieving control over polarization is crucial in various fields like spintronics and nonlinear optics. Recent advancements in nanostructures and polarization control have opened doors to novel applications and devices operating at terahertz frequencies. This research introduces a cutting-edge method for polarizing terahertz radiation using nanostructured monolayers of transition metal dichalcogenides. By manipulating the polarization of individual layers, the researchers were able to generate terahertz radiation with high circular polarization, exceeding 99% efficiency in a specific direction. Notably, this technique can be adjusted to produce linear polarization by aligning the nanostructures at a 90-degree angle.

This study investigates the generalised Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equation $u_t = \Delta \lambda \gamma (u) + \beta \gamma'(u) \cdot \nabla u + \mu \gamma''(u) \cdot \Delta u + \lambda \gamma (u) + \mu \gamma''(u) + \lambda \gamma (u) + f(x,t)$ within an open bounded domain $\Omega$ of C^2 smoothness, featuring a nonlinear reaction term $\gamma$. Given the parameters $\lambda$ and $\mu$, both of which are small and non-negative, we establish the existence and non-existence of solutions under specific conditions on $\gamma$ and the driving force $f(x,t)$.

The COVID-19 pandemic has brought significant disruption to South Africa, a country struggling with diverse data accessibility issues. Certain publicly available data are marred by inconsistencies and data protection concerns, while other essential datasets are inaccessible due to data ownership and contractual restrictions. To address these challenges, the South African Data Science for COVID-19 (DS4C) initiative aims to coordinate data access and harmonize regulations, ultimately facilitating responsible data sharing and usage. This effort aligns with international best practices, as embodied by the World Health Organization's Data Governance Framework, and has already begun engaging with local stakeholders to establish a standardized data access platform.

We investigate how allowing a limited number of terms in the sum influences the characteristics of subsets of integers regarding their inclusion within arithmetic progressions. Specifically, we establish an lower bound on how restricted sums of a limited nature within the integers can be, under certain conditions. This is achieved by formulating an equivalent problem in a combinatorial game, which we prove to have a minimum value of at least $2^{\Omega(n^\alpha)}$, by employing a hybrid strategy combining the Hypperplane Covering conjecture with a recent result by Green-Tao and Pudlák. Here, the exponent $\alpha$ is determined by the interplay between the conjecture and Pudlák's result, which both yield different values for $\alpha$ in the range $[1/2,1/2+\varepsilon]$, where $\varepsilon>0$.

Hierarchical fusion techniques are gaining traction as early and intermediate approaches have limitations in combining non-hierarchical sources of information. In this paper, we introduce a new hierarchical fusion model, addressing the lack of comprehensive assessment methods for its performance. We propose a metric that quantifies the degree of hierarchy in fusion techniques and conduct a thorough evaluation of the hierarchical model using this metric. Additionally, we compare the performance of the hierarchical model with popular early and intermediate fusion methods, considering multiple training and feature extraction techniques.

The COVID-19 pandemic's severity varies across regions, leading to unpredictable hospital resource shortages. To address this, we propose a novel framework for long-term ICU demand forecasting, enabling healthcare systems to allocate and prepare for required resources in advance. By leveraging data from public health databases, our framework models the co-occurrence of specific patient features and ICU admissions, allowing for more accurate and resource-constrained predictions. The feasibility of our approach is demonstrated using data from New York State's COVID-19 report, where we analyze the probability of specific patient features and ICU admission, ultimately informing resource allocation decisions.

We investigate the most efficiently transmitted transmission eigenfunctions within the scope of the Dirichlet problem for the steady-state Helmholtz equation in a $N$-dimensional ball. By assuming the medium's properties vary smoothly, except for two constant regions, we demonstrate that these functions concentrate near the boundary of the domain $\Omega$, as the frequency $\Lambda$ tends to infinity. Our analysis yields an explicit estimate of the concentration rate, in addition to a uniform bound on the eigenfunctions' values.

To enhance representation learning of spoken words, we examine how various
multi-task training techniques contribute to the representation of individual
utterances. Specifically, we investigate three methods: modifying the
loss function, adding contrastive learning, and introducing a new task. Our
analysis involves a pre-trained model that has been trained on a specific
dataset, and we evaluate the impact of these methods by comparing the
performance of a downstream task using both a supervised and self-supervised
approach. Our results indicate that the method that adds a new task yields the
highest improvement in representation of individual utterances.

The Bergman functor Berg maps any monad T to a subfunctor U of the universal bundle functor PB associated with the free group functor G. It's shown here that U represents a coreflexive subfunctor of PB. As a result, the first component of the Bergman functor corresponds to a coreflexive subfunctor of the universal path fibration for groups, which can be described as the functor mapping any group to its maximal abelian subgroup enclosed within its Mal'cev closure.

The total number of subgroups within a finite group $G$ of order $n$ is directly proportional to $n^{\omega(G)}$, where the exponent $\omega(G)$ results from applying a specific mathematical formula to group $G$.

We demonstrate that the continuum limit of the $S^{(1,0)}$ variable from the discrete Korteweg-de Vries hierarchy corresponds to a non-standard dressing of the Korteweg-de Vries soliton solution. The dressing involves a non-zero limit of the lattice parameter 'c' in the dressing transformation.

Optimizing models for Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) is hindered by the slow convergence caused by biased gradient estimation due to incorrect framing of the two-norm. To address this, we introduce Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), a straightforward yet effective strategy that mitigates the issue by uniformly sampling both positive and negative examples. BNPS accelerates model optimization and improves convergence in experiments.

A recent study introduced a novel approach to determine residual quantumness in a quantum system using weak measurements. This led to the development of an iterative method to iteratively release and measure quantumness. In this research, we demonstrate that this process fails to yield the desired outcome as quantumness is preserved throughout. In contrast, our findings indicate that weak measurement by-products cannot fully extract residual quantumness, and we provide a counterexample to show that such a protocol cannot function. Nevertheless, we propose an alternative strategy to iteratively eliminate quantumness using strong measurements.

In recent years, social relationship analysis has become a significant field of study, enabling researchers to better understand individual connections on a large scale. This work presents a novel method for updating social relationship states on a graph by incorporating a recurrent neural network. Specifically, we utilize Gated Recurrent Units to capture local relationship changes and leverage Matrix Multiplication as a parameter-efficient mechanism for aggregating adjacent nodes' attributes. This approach is further demonstrated by the model's application in a specific task, achieving comparable results to state-of-the-art methods in predicting friendships on a Facebook dataset.

Graph neural networks utilize spatially localized message passing to process node attributes, but their applicability is constrained by their O(N) complexity, where N represents the number of nodes. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel approach, node sampling, to accelerate GNNs. By selectively training a subset of nodes, we achieve a substantial reduction in computational complexity to O(sqrt(N)). Our method is further enhanced through adaptive node selection, allowing it to skip unnecessary training. Our experiments demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in accelerating GNNs on multiple datasets.

In the design of Multiple Constant Multiplication circuits, the method used to pass errors affects their correctness. Current approaches rely on cumbersome proof mechanisms to validate the design process. To address this issue, we develop a set of error propagation rules that enables efficient formal verification of the design process. We also introduce a formal framework for verifying MCMLs and provide a concrete implementation of our approach, demonstrating its applicability through successful verification of various MCML examples.

The rapidly evolving field of quantum deep learning holds great promise for 
advancing machine learning through quantum computing's unique capabilities. 
Despite significant research progress, quantum deep learning still faces several 
challenges, including the development of efficient quantum algorithms for large 
data sets and reliable quantum hardware. This article provides an in-depth look 
at the current state of quantum deep learning and future research directions.

In recent years, advancements in radio frequency (RF) technology have been driven by high-energy physics applications, but have also found widespread use in other fields such as medicine, astronomy, and defense. This paper examines the technological progress within the European accelerator community, focusing on innovations that have been developed and implemented at CERN over the past decade. The discussion is then broadened to include advancements outside of high-energy physics, highlighting notable examples and their applications.

This report presents the initial findings from the Muon Collider R&D Task Force, which outline the design and implementation difficulties, technical complexities, and various research and development priorities for a high-energy muon collider.

We examine the theoretical frameworks of kinetic theory and fluid dynamics with a non-conservative approach, both modeling relativistic fluids with viscosity. By comparing the underlying equations for these theories, we identify a non-conservative fluid dynamics model that is equivalent to kinetic theory's Boltzmann equation with a specific collision term. We then analyze the linear perturbations of these theories, specifically looking at fluid dynamics under both conservative and non-conservative assumptions, and find that the former yields different scalar and vector mode dispersion relations than the non-conservative approach. In contrast, we find that the non-conservative fluid dynamics model is kinetically consistent, with both the non-conservative and conservative fluid dynamics approaches being thermodynamically consistent.

Primordial black holes that form from cosmic perturbations can act as highly efficient photon detectors, emitting Hawking radiation at extremely low energies. This phenomenon occurs because the peak energy of Hawking radiation is directly proportional to the mass of the primordial black holes. Consequently, a large number of these black holes would produce a significant low-energy photon flux that could be detectable. Notably, this effect is more pronounced for lighter primordial black holes, which are more abundant according to certain theoretical models. In this study, we explore the possibility of observing this low-energy radiation using advanced astrophysical detectors.

This paper presents a novel approach to parallel processing, where a pipelined architecture-based processor executes a circuit with a high number of inputs and outputs in no time. The time complexity of this processing method is remarkably improved, from an original O(N) to o(N^(1+delta)), with delta being a positive value less than 1. The paper also outlines a step-by-step procedure to construct a suitable processor for any given circuit.

We have derived a precise approximation algorithm for solving minimization problems with general-valued constraint satisfaction, involving specific constraints such as linear and quadratic functions. The PTAS applies to instances with limited occurrences of large values and can be extended to scenarios with limited occurrences of a specified range of values. The PTAS works by initially identifying and approximating the most influential variables, then recursively solving the problem on a reduced instance of the problem. The variable importance is determined by evaluating the constraint functions, and we have developed methods to efficiently approximate these functions for linear and quadratic constraints.

This study introduces FPIO, a few-shot parsing model that outperforms previous few-shot parsing approaches even when trained with just ten annotated examples. FPIO achieves this performance by leveraging a novel combination of self-supervised pre-training and a probabilistic model. The model's self-supervised technique generates synthetic data in the form of node pairs, which allows it to learn rich representations of program structure. During the inference process, FPIO utilizes these representations in a probabilistic model to derive tree structures from source code, thereby taking program structure's uncertainty into account. The model's probabilistic nature also enables it to provide confidence levels for its predictions, which can be utilized to filter out unlikely results. Evaluations on various datasets indicate that FPIO offers superior results compared to existing few-shot parsing methods.

High-dimensional hyperspectral images offer precise spectral data that can be leveraged to enhance semantic segmentation, surpassing the limitations of conventional RGB images. This study investigates how refined labels from hyperspectral images influence the performance of semantic segmentation, revealing that segmentation improves significantly when the color space is reduced. Additionally, we identify a spectral correlation threshold, approximately 0.25, that serves as a criterion for effective label enhancement. This finding implies that, for most datasets, the benefits of hyperspectral imaging are largely rooted in its spectral dimensions rather than its high-dimensional space.

Our research focused on the star KIC 9267654, an object that had been identified as a gamma Doradus variable due to its unique observation patterns. We analyzed the star's properties using data from the Kepler space telescope and additional spectroscopic information. The results revealed a rotation rate that significantly increased with latitude, an unusual phenomenon that defies explanation with existing theories. The observed behavior cannot be fully accounted for by the star's convective zone or magnetic field effects. We propose the presence of a toroidal magnetic field as a potential factor that could influence the star's behavior.

We introduce a randomized algorithm for solving the shortest path problem on undirected graphs with Hedges and Koutsiouidis' efficient round lower bound of O(log^2 n), applying the black-box shortest paths technique by Zwick. Our implementation achieves a deterministic time complexity of O(n^omega log^2 n) by incorporating a novel randomized linear system solver with a new Monte Carlo algorithm for the approximate shortest path oracle problem. This solver can be integrated into multiple other frameworks, including an earlier one by Zwick for a time complexity of O(log^2 n), all under the condition that the graph's hopscotch diameter is at most poly(log n).

Self-supervised learning has gained significant traction in session-based recommendation systems, enhancing data representation by leveraging interactions within a session. However, existing self-supervised methods primarily focus on session-level representations, neglecting the benefits of target item augmentation. To address this, we introduce a novel self-supervised approach that combines group and pair-level augmentations. By grouping multiple sessions and applying a contrastive learning technique, we optimize aggregated representations. Subsequently, we employ target item augmentation through a self-supervised loss function. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in various evaluation metrics.

Group ring code design presents various challenges due to the diverse properties of group ring elements. The selection of group ring elements significantly impacts the code's properties. This paper delves into the characteristics of LCD codes constructed using group ring elements under the condition that the sum of two group ring elements equals a unit. The study also presents a method to create full-length binary LCD codes based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem.

Using the properties of invariant differential forms, we compute the real cohomology in the stable range for the general linear group over a local field of characteristic zero. Specifically, we find that the real cohomology can be broken down into a sum of individual components resulting from a particular class of forms.

In recent years, RNNs have demonstrated exceptional performance in object
categorization, particularly when augmented with auxiliary variables. This
study delves into the essential role of these auxiliary variables, revealing
that they serve to facilitate learning within the RNN itself, rather than in
previous interpretations, where their effect was mainly attributed to an
improved representation of input data. To validate this finding, the
researchers analyzed the internal workings of the RNN layer by examining its
activation patterns across different layers within a deep architecture.
Surprisingly, the results show that the auxiliary variables are most actively
engaged when the network is not yet certain about its classification output,
suggesting a connection to the concept of uncertainty in Bayesian models.
Furthermore, the study provides a mathematical explanation for how the auxiliary
variables can be perceived as a manifestation of the network's uncertainty,
illustrating this effect with a simple example in a 2D classification task.

In non-Hermitian systems, the skin effect has been found to occur even in topologically non-trivial scenarios. This phenomenon is observed in a non-Hermitian model known as the Hatano-Nelson chain when it is modified to include longer-range hopping. By analyzing the non-Hermitian localized bulk states within this model, we derive an analytical expression that quantifies the extent of the skin effect. This derivation reveals that the skin effect is influenced by the interplay between hopping distances and non-reciprocity, decreasing as the difference between hopping distances increases. Additionally, our findings indicate that the skin effect can be minimized by adjusting the relative non-reciprocity levels at shorter-range sites.

This study establishes the criteria under which a quaternary Golay complementary array pair exists, comprising GPCAs with indices (m, n) and (m+1, n+1). Additionally, the investigation also sets the standards for the existence of quaternary narrow-sense idempotent complementary array pairs, consisting of NCAs with indices (m, n) and (m+1, n+1).

We've analyzed Higgs boson interactions with vector bosons using diphoton and four-lepton data from the LHC, between 7 and 13 TeV. Our findings reveal that deviations from standard model predictions are constrained at the 10^-16 GeV^2 level for the dominant anomalous dimensions. The analysis also yields constraints on the standard model effective lagrangian parameters, with certain combinations restricted at the 10^-16 GeV^4 level.

This study offers a comprehensive examination of change detection in unsupervised remote sensing change, contrasting it with traditional supervised approaches. We assess the efficacy of four cutting-edge change detection techniques: self-supervised learning, autoencoders, cluster-based change detection, and the adaptive region-based technique. We also investigate how these methods compare to more established reference methods in various scenarios. Notably, we demonstrate that unsupervised change detection can outperform supervised techniques, requiring neither manual labeling nor background knowledge. Moreover, we show that the adaptive region-based method excels in several metrics and is computationally efficient.

We've refined W. Schwarz's finding, now we have that $e^{\eta^2/2}\ll_{\eta} n^{1/4-\eta}$ holds true for any $\eta>0$, which in turn gives us a more accurate version of his initial asymptotic formula. This new formula provides a more precise estimate for the count of representations of natural numbers as sums of squares and additive complements, surpassing the previous result by a factor of $\sqrt{n}$.

Silicon's Heisenberg spin exchange interaction can be manipulated by introducing impurities at specific sites, resulting in various direct and indirect interactions. By analyzing the four-band model of silicon with non-magnetic impurities, we identify conditions under which the indirect exchange via a common host electron can occur. The conditions include the positioning of the impurities, located at next-nearest neighbor sites, in the <100> direction. The strength of the indirect exchange interaction is found to be comparable to the direct one, and it can be influenced by the spin splitting. The discovery of a novel, indirect exchange mechanism paves the way for the development of quantum spin devices within silicon.

The open-source C library, LibOPT, is a collection of benchmarking functions that can be used to evaluate, compare, and adapt optimization algorithms across various domains. It currently offers 25 benchmarking functions, each with a diverse range of characteristics, such as unimodal, multimodal, continuous, and integer functions. Additionally, the library includes a random function generator that enables the creation of custom benchmarking functions on-the-fly. This allows researchers to easily create and share their own optimized variants of existing benchmarking functions. LibOPT is distributed under the Permissive BSD-3 License and is available for download at libopt.software.institute.org.

This research calculates the transitivity degree of geometrically invariant subsets on specific algebraic varieties, such as Grassmannians and Quotients of Schubert varieties within these varieties, as defined by the action of general linear groups.

We're expanding on a previous work that established a quantum framework for defining total momentum in non-abelian systems. This time, we're deriving a formula for the total momentum of a single particle or a group of particles within a specific boundary. We're applying this formula to a model featuring interacting gluons and one or more quarks. We're also discussing how to obtain the total momentum of a quantum system from its constituent particles.

We investigate the interaction between light and a two-dimensional semiconductor using a model that incorporates both two-photon absorption and multiple carrier generation via impact excitation. By developing a mathematical description, we derive a set of coupled equations that govern the behavior of light and charge carriers within the material. These equations enable us to analyze the influence of two-photon absorption and determine the threshold for laser light propagation within the material. Our findings also highlight the significance of impact excitation in a three-dimensional manner on two-photon photonic crystal slab behavior.

We've developed a novel approach to detecting misogynistic language that leverages large-scale language models. Our system consists of two key components: a MARBERT-based classifier and a sentence transformer. The former utilizes contextualized representations to identify misogynistic text, while the latter enables these representations to be captured across entire sentences. The classifier's effectiveness is further enhanced by utilizing the model's pre-trained word representations. Our method surpasses the performance of current state-of-the-art detectors, achieving a score of 0.9839 F1, as validated on the 2020 SemEval14 Hate Speech Identification task's English dataset.

This study examines a type of backward stochastic differential equation that incorporates historical data in its definition, a concept previously explored in the context of forward BSDEs by Bao, Yan, and Yuan. We establish the existence and uniqueness of adapted solutions under specific assumptions and show that including past values in the generator makes solvability more robust, even if the generator exhibits path-dependent characteristics.

In order to improve the reliability of controllers that learn through trial and error, we suggest adding a minimum level of uncertainty to a model that predicts dynamics. This increased uncertainty helps a conservative controller to take the unpredictable aspects of the predictions into account, which in turn leads the controller to develop more robust policies. We tested this idea on a simple target-following task in a complex environment and found that requiring the predictions to be at least that uncertain in a probabilistic sense significantly boosted the controller's ability to withstand disturbances and adapt to changes in the environment without compromising its performance.

This paper proposes a unified framework for generating coded caching schemes by linking various existing methods to relevant combinatorial concepts. Leveraging this framework, we establish a direct connection between different caching approaches and identify key relationships between them.

We've developed a constructive and predicative framework for studying type theories with specific computational and computational types. Our framework is based on the Scott model, which is particularly well-suited for handling type theories with specific computational and computational types. We've demonstrated that several type theories, including those with the TCF and FCF introduced by Cohen, Coquand, and others, can be represented within our framework. We've also shown that this representation preserves key properties of the original type theories.

This study introduces an advanced computational tool for calculating the values of degenerate Eisenstein series at a specific point based on the representation theory of the general linear group. We have developed algorithms to determine the precise values of certain components within the series, specifically those related to the residual cosets of the Weyl group, under the given parameters of $GL_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$.

This study introduces a new method for creating safe motion plans on a mobile robotic arm. Our approach generates control policies that account for the robot's shape and location, ensuring seamless avoidance of obstacles. By transforming this problem into a discrete-time linear problem, we derive a control strategy that can be efficiently implemented. Our method is now available in open-source form and outperforms existing methods in relevant benchmarks.

This report introduces a fundamental NLP system, which processes data to create models that can be applied across various tasks. We utilize diverse language patterns, including written and spoken inputs, to overcome limitations in current NLP technology.

A theoretical study on improving Ramsey interferometry with Bose-Einstein condensates is presented, utilizing a nonlinear Hadamard gate to increase its precision. Initially, a quantum state is created by the Hadamard gate and then separated in time for Ramsey interferometry to measure its nonlinear effects. These effects are observed in the Ramsey signal's phase space evolution, which shows a transition from coherent to incoherent states. Notably, the nonlinear gate significantly enhances the interferometry's precision, surpassing its linear counterpart.

This paper explores various problems and findings concerning meromorphic mappings from a non-normal complex projective space to another, involving specific constraints related to hypersurfaces and hyperplanes within these spaces.

In signature-based Gröbner basis methods, the Gröbner basis is computed for each polynomial system subset, based on a predetermined order of variables. This specialized approach is adapted for parametric polynomial systems, where each coefficient is considered a variable, and the Gröbner basis is computed for various variable subsets in a specific order. A previous method computed the Gröbner basis for these subsets using a pre-determined order, but we have developed a new method that determines the most beneficial variable subsets order to reduce computation time and memory usage.

The PHENIX Collaboration has measured direct photon production in Cu+Cu collisions at an energy of 200 GeV per nucleon pair. By analyzing the underlying event density, the collaboration found that the rapidity density of photons in Cu+Cu collisions is 1.04 ± 0.28 (stat.) ± 0.05 (syst.) lower than in Au+Au collisions at the same energy, but 1.29 ± 0.27 (stat.) ± 0.05 (syst.) higher than in Pb+Pb collisions at 2.76 TeV. The collaboration also determined that the transverse momentum spectrum of direct photons in Cu+Cu collisions follows the same trend as in Au+Au and Pb+Pb collisions, but with a suppression relative to the next-to-leading order perturbative QCD prediction that is 0.75 ± 0.08 (stat.) ± 0.07 (syst.) lower than in Au+Au collisions, but 1.04 ± 0.13 (stat.) ± 0.10 (syst.) higher than in Pb+Pb collisions.

We introduce a new property, exco_2(n,H), which represents the maximum size of a 4-hypergraph without the H structure containing at most n vertices. This property is similar to ex(n,H), which was first defined by Erdos in 1963, but uses a different type of graph structure. By examining the exco_2(n,H) property, we find upper limits for its value and prove multiple theorems related to it. These theorems have implications for other graph properties, such as those studied by Frankl and Tokushige.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for rendering text and line artwork, specifically addressing a long-standing issue of thin line join imperfections. The proposed method employs a new fan-shaped polygon creation technique that accurately represents the intended visual effect, resulting in a significant improvement over prior approaches. Furthermore, the paper outlines a strategy for applying the join rendering algorithm to various line types, including cursive and dot-dash patterns. The proposed algorithm has been implemented and demonstrated in the free, open-source vector graphics editor Inkscape.

This paper presents a quasi-interpolation formula based on a novel radial basis function (RBF) that combines positivity and convexity. Unlike traditional RBF interpolation which can lose its convexity when translated, our approach maintains convexity and monotonicity while allowing for translations without loss of these properties.

Pulsar halos, formed through the dispersal of pulsar wind bubbles, can provide valuable insights into the long-term history of pulsar creation within the Galactic plane. These structures are associated with a localized excess of cosmic positrons and may also contribute to the diffuse TeV gamma-ray excess observed by the MAGIC telescope. We employ a Monte Carlo simulation to investigate the detectability of pulsar halos through gamma-ray observations, assuming a typical gamma-ray spectrum. Utilizing a detailed model of pulsar distribution, we identify potential locations for pulsar halos and determine that the Fermi-LAT is capable of detecting approximately 20 such structures within its field of view. However, these halos may be difficult to distinguish from other gamma-ray sources due to their low signal strength.

Recent advancements in machine learning, particularly in data-hungry deep learning techniques, have highlighted a significant limitation - their poor generalization abilities outside of the training dataset. To address this issue, researchers have explored various data enhancement methods that modify input data and force models to learn more robust features. In this study, we focus on using super pixel delimiting masks as a data augmentation technique to improve the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in image classification tasks. By doing so, we aim to answer whether this method is beneficial and, if so, which aspects of CNNs it influences.

This study examines the temporal progression of climate change in prominent academic journals and reveals the findings through a comparative analysis of search engine trends. The results indicate that the interest of policymakers in climate change lags behind that of economists and general interest science journals, yet surpasses the interest of scientists. The data also show that the primary focus of policymakers' research is on mitigation, whereas scientists and economists focus on adaptation.

This research introduces a novel control strategy for a specific class of soft robotic joints, utilizing the properties of the Koopman operator theory. The specific joint is modeled as a nonlinear system, but the control problem is redefined as a linear quadratic regulator with algebraic path constraints. Due to the system's nonlinearities, traditional methods fail to obtain the optimal control solution, but we overcome this by applying the Koopman operator theory to linearize the control problem. The resulting paradigm allows us to break down the original control problem into smaller, more manageable pieces, which can then be solved using existing solutions for linear systems. The novel approach is compared to state-of-the-art methods on a soft robotic finger, demonstrating superior performance in terms of solution accuracy.

JaxGDN is a Python implementation of the Natural Gradient Descent method, which accelerates conventional optimization techniques by achieving faster convergence speeds. Developed based on the original research paper, this implementation is versatile and adaptable to various models and loss functions. JaxGDN is specifically designed for use with the JAX library, which it requires for execution.

We've identified a notable AGN, designated as QSO 1225+7191 at a redshift of 5.84, which exhibits a unique feature. Using the JWST/NIRCam images, we've discovered a dusty feature with a size of approximately 500 parsecs, which appears as a distinct arc and multiple spots. These features were observed in various wavelengths, from 1.5 to 4.8 micrometers, where they display distinct colors. We've analyzed the spectral behavior of these features using the F160W, F200W, and MIRI/GTO features, which show a notable increase in wavelength. These features are characterized by a low dust temperature of around 150 Kelvin, which suggests a high dust-to-gas ratio. We propose that these features are composed of dense molecular clouds, which are likely to be associated with the host galaxy. These clouds are situated near the AGN, which may be responsible for their ionization. We've estimated that these clouds are massive, with a total mass of approximately 10^8 solar masses, which is consistent with the predicted cloud masses at high redshifts.

This study introduces Lite-ProSENet, a compact and efficient model derived from ProSENet, which significantly outperforms the original model in survival analysis for lung cancer by a substantial margin, achieving a 10% improvement in AUC. Lite-ProSENet boasts a notably lower parameter count, 0.81% fewer parameters than EfficientNet-B7, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

Achieving linguistically meaningful state representations is crucial for various tasks, such as natural language instruction following and storytelling. However, current sequence-to-sequence models often generate human-like output sequences without providing insight into their internal state representations. To address this, we propose a novel framework that combines the advantages of semantic frame-based models and sequence-to-sequence models, enabling the development of state representations that are both linguistically and computationally interpretable.

We've developed a new approach to reconstructing the power spectrum from cosmological data, allowing for an accurate estimate of its uncertainty. This method is versatile and can be applied across various scales, from large to small, without being restricted to specific types of data. We've tested its performance using a synthetic survey of galaxy clusters, similar to actual surveys like SPTpol and CRESST, and found that its accuracy improves as higher-wavelength data is included. We've also demonstrated its effectiveness in a general case, using a synthetic signal with a specific shape, and found that its results are comparable to those obtained with more sophisticated techniques, such as MPCube.

We derive a criterion to establish if the tensor product of a highest weight module, U(𝕙)-free module, and another module is irreducible, by showing it is reducible if and only if it is isomorphic to a specific type of module. Additionally, we use this criterion to identify all irreducible U(𝕁ₙ) modules with a given dominant weight.

This research paper presents a Twitter sentiment analysis model based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which was found to be highly effective in classifying tweet sentiment with an impressive 95.96% accuracy rate. Building upon existing work in the field, we enhanced the LSTM model by integrating word2vec and skip gram embedding to improve its performance. Additionally, we compared its efficacy with other state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms.

The characteristics of interlocutors' roles significantly influence the performance of a dialogue system, yet current studies rarely consider role specifications in their training and evaluation. To address this limitation, we introduce a new dataset, Role-Specified Dialogue Dataset (RSD), which includes natural conversations with clearly defined roles. We also propose an approach, Role-Spec Augmentation (RSA), to enhance the diversity of dialogue training data by incorporating role information. Experimental results demonstrate that both role specification awareness and data augmentation methods contribute to improved dialogue generation quality.

The residual distortions left behind by the sources' positions in gravitational waves are often disregarded due to their insignificance in most scenarios. However, these residual effects could potentially form a significant background in specific situations, such as from inspiraling binary systems or the early universe. This background, known as stochastic gravitational wave memory, differs from the standard background, which is caused by the sources' variations in mass and energy emission. Notably, the memory background exhibits a distinct frequency behavior. In this study, we explore the properties of this memory background, specifically its spectral density, and establish a method to calculate it for arbitrary source distributions. Our findings are demonstrated through two particular source configurations: an inspiraling binary system similar to those observed in our galaxy, and a cosmic phase transition occurring at a high redshift.

We've developed a supersymmetry model that uses gauge-mediated breaking, resulting in a PeV-scale leptogenesis outcome. This model naturally prevents rapid proton decay due to non-renormalizable operators, yielding proton lifetimes significantly exceeding current experimental limits. Additionally, we've determined the required parameters for successful leptogenesis within the context of the seesaw mechanism, specifically within its type-I and type-II variations.

This study introduces a novel air-to-ground communication framework that utilizes a machine learning approach to enhance semantic integrity in wireless data transmission. The proposed Extra Semantic Check (ESC) system leverages deep learning to monitor and detect errors caused by fading and MIMO interference, providing more reliable wireless data transmission than conventional methods. In contrast to traditional data integrity checks, the ESC system evaluates the semantic consistency of received information, rather than focusing on data verification. The ESC system's semantic reliability is mathematically modeled and its performance is evaluated under various fading conditions, demonstrating its superior error-detection capabilities.

We introduce HyMS, a hybrid model for word suggestion that integrates semantic and syntactic information. In contrast to earlier approaches, HyMS has been designed to handle out-of-vocabulary words without requiring them to be part of the model's training data. The model's performance in open-vocabulary settings is on par with its in-vocabulary performance, making it a more practical solution for real-world applications. The results show that HyMS surpasses the efficacy of models relying solely on syntactic or semantic analysis, and its variants outperform the current state-of-the-art models in various evaluation metrics.

To enhance the ranking of recommended items, we propose using attention networks to prioritize relevant information. The proposed method, called Net-Attention, integrates net-like attention mechanisms into recommendation systems by incorporating multiple parallel layers of attention circuits. Net-Attention is applied to various scenarios of recommender systems and outperforms existing methods in multiple experiments.

Active dimers composed of a stiff rod and a soft joint can move when driven by an oscillating force, mirroring the effect of a steering wheel in larger vehicles. By analyzing their behavior, we discover that this type of motion is influenced by a critical parameter that signifies a sudden change from one stable state to another. In our study, we also explore the possibility of controlling these dimers using an external signal and find that this can be achieved through a specific driving method that results in predictable outcomes.

We introduce a novel mesh generation algorithm that leverages an optimized tetrahedralization framework, specifically designed for simulations of media with fractures. This technique ensures that generated meshes conform to given fractures and remain valid by avoiding degenerate cases. Building upon a previous mesh generation approach, our method employs a mesh modification procedure to produce high-quality meshes. The key innovation lies in incorporating an efficient mesh validation protocol, which enables the algorithm to create well-conditioned tetrahedralizations in complex fracture scenarios.

This research proposes an efficient method to decrease the deviation of a drone swarm's centroid from a pre-defined target location. The centroid deviation problem is initially framed as an optimization issue, with several alternative formulations presented along with their computational complexities. A novel approach is introduced to solve this problem, which involves dividing the task into two simpler optimization tasks. The results of this method are then compared with those of a genetic algorithm solution. The research also demonstrates through simulation that the proposed strategy outperforms a method that aims to maintain a constant centroid distance from the target.

This paper explores the Seidel matrix spectrum for a specific type of graph: the connected chain graph. It's proven that -1 is a unique eigenvalue, and additional eigenvalues are complex conjugate pairs. A closed formula has been found for the Seidel matrix eigenvalues, along with the corresponding eigenvectors.

This study investigates the optimal consumption problem for a power utility function, considering both a delay and the uncertainty of a regime-switching market. We employ a combination of two approaches to resolve the issue: first, we leverage an operator algebra to address the delay; second, we utilize a stochastic control method to account for the uncertainty of the market. Our analysis yields a closed-loop feedback strategy, providing a clear consumption plan. Notably, the impact of the delay is analogous to the effect of a specific parameter in the market model, which we derive mathematically.

We establish a connection between the eigenvalue problems for the Dirac operator and solutions to Heun's equation, also linking the resulting operators to a specific class of tridiagonal operators. This allows us to apply the known spectral findings related to the spectral theory of Jacobi operators to the Dirac operator.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of a complex vehicular communication network that comprises multiple types of road users, relay deployments, and varied channel conditions. Leveraging stochastic geometry, we develop a spatially aware model to assess performance in this network. Specifically, we investigate how relay placement affects the overall communication quality and derive a general expression for the metric. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of relay deployment strategies on users of different types and numerically demonstrate their influence.

Wikipedia editors' input can be leveraged to enhance sentence quality labeling, a crucial task. By analyzing Wikipedia edit histories, we discovered that editors' editing patterns of specific sentences can serve as a reliable indicator of those sentences' quality. Focusing on German Wikipedia, we created a dataset consisting of sentences paired with their corresponding editing characteristics and a quality label. This dataset was utilized to train a classifier, which outperformed existing methods in predicting sentence quality. Moreover, our approach allows for the identification of high-quality sentences that have remained unchanged in Wikipedia, making them suitable for pre-training language models and other applications.

Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that involves training a smaller model to mimic the output of a larger model. Black-box knowledge distillation, in particular, does not require the large model's training data. Recent research introduced decision-based black-box knowledge distillation, which uses a query-based approach to obtain teacher outputs. This method is distinct from traditional knowledge distillation, as it does not rely on the teacher's training data or network architecture. Notably, decision-based black-box knowledge distillation can be applied even after the teacher model has undergone training. This paper presents an improved version of the method, incorporating various enhancements, such as ensemble and weighted teacher architectures. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of these modifications.

A comprehensive analysis of $B^0_s \to D^{\mp} \pi^{\mp}$ decays is conducted, where the decay modes include $D^0 D^0$, $D^{\pm} \pi^{\mp}$, and $D^0 \pi^0$ pairs. The study utilizes a 3.0 fb$^{-1}$ dataset collected by the LHCb detector operating at a 7 TeV centre-of-mass energy. The branching fractions for the $B^0_s \to D^{\mp} \pi^{\mp}$ decay modes are measured relative to the $B^0 \to D^{\mp} \pi^{\mp}$ processes, yielding absolute branching fraction ranges of 0.25% to 0.64% and 0.59% to 1.09% for the $B^0_s \to D^{\mp} \pi^{\mp}$ and $B^0 \to D^{\mp} \pi^{\mp}$ decay modes, respectively.

In non-geometric string theory, often encountered in scenarios involving strongly-deformed branes, geometric realizations of such models are typically found to lack classical T-duals. However, we demonstrate that this non-existence is a direct consequence of a specific algebraic property within the double-brane sector, known as a continuous-trace algebra. This leads us to propose an alternative, geometric interpretation of the non-geometric double, postulating the existence of a classical T-dual.

A novel learning paradigm, co-imitation learning, enables a learner agent to mimic both a teacher agent's actions and its own past experiences. This approach is particularly beneficial when teacher input is scarce or impractical to obtain. We investigate the theoretical underpinnings of co-imitation learning in the context of Markov decision processes and identify both successes and limitations. A key challenge arises from the learner's tendency to overfit the teacher's behavior, which can be mitigated by introducing a regularization term to encourage diversity in the learner's actions.

This research investigates the performance of a discrete memoryless channel under a sequential maximal-a-posteriori (MAP) decoding scheme. The decoder's error probability is analyzed in relation to a cutoff rate, which is calculated based on the channel's polarization characteristics. The study demonstrates that the error probability is influenced by the specific polarization rate utilized to determine the cutoff rate. Nevertheless, when the cutoff rate is set at the maximum achievable rate, the error probability is found to be consistently high across varying channel conditions. Conversely, when the cutoff rate is established using a polarized cutoff rate, the error probability is shown to be low, amounting to no more than 0.1, under typical channel scenarios.

This paper introduces a novel approach for tracking hands and objects interacting within a PASCAL dataset, specifically designed for scenarios where hands obscure from view. Our method employs a distinct object representation based on a sparse set of key points and incorporates an occlusion filter to mitigate identification issues. To improve accuracy, we utilize a limited number of efficient support vectors to represent the appearance of tracked items. Our approach outperforms existing solutions in experiments and is notably more efficient, taking roughly 0.25ms per frame.

We have obtained complete classifications for reduced groups over a finite field GL(n, q), classifying them by isomorphism. Specifically, we found that GL(n, q) is completely classified when n is 2 or 3, but this classification is incomplete for higher dimensions. However, we did provide a key step in this direction by classifying a significant subset of reduced groups within GL(n, q).

This study introduces a novel method for enhancing the accuracy of end-effector pose calculation during the calibration process. Our approach leverages a depth camera in conjunction with an end-effector tracker to establish the end-effector's reference frame. A key aspect of this method is its ability to adapt and correct large-scale errors without the need for manual intervention. To achieve this, we developed an optimization algorithm that integrates data from both the depth camera and the tracker. Notably, our method is distinct from existing calibration techniques, which typically rely on a calibrated camera as the primary reference for end-effector pose calculation. Instead, our solution utilizes a combination of data to determine the end-effector's pose. We evaluated our method in simulated environments and on a robotic arm, demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating calibration-related issues.

Conducting experiments to measure actual network interference is complicated by the numerous hidden variables involved. To address this, we suggest a method to identify the most relevant units for interference in an experiment. By focusing on the specific units with the greatest impact, we can collect data more efficiently. The performance of our approach is compared to a leading alternative using a large dataset from wireless networking experiments, revealing a significant improvement in data collection speed without compromising accuracy.

The presence of dark matter in a neutron star can be confirmed by analyzing its cooling pattern. This is because, unlike ordinary matter, dark matter cannot be created or destroyed through nuclear reactions, so its effect on the star's cooling process is straightforward. In this study, we explore the possibility of a type of dark matter called self-annihilating weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) existing within a neutron star.
